subject: Next steps: procurement route & marketplace preference (CloudScale Analytics)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudscale.io>, Tom Hayes <t.hayes@cloudscale.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: Next steps: procurement route & marketplace preference (CloudScale Analytics)

Hi Lena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on your ML platform use case and the initial pilot scope. Quick recap and a few action items so procurement can evaluate the right purchase path (marketplace vs PO / card):

What we covered (brief)
- Pilot: 3-node inference footprint, expected ~200k tokens/day peak, 30k tokens/day avg
- Compliance: SOC2 + optional VPC/private deployment for regulated workloads
- Success criteria: latency under 200ms p50 and cost per inference target

Open questions for procurement evaluation
1) Preferred purchase channel: do you have a hard preference for AWS Marketplace vs corporate PO (net 30) vs corporate card for initial pilot?
2) If Marketplace is preferred, is your procurement team already registered as an AWS Marketplace buyer or will they need seller/contract details?
3) If using PO, does CloudScale require vendor paperwork (W9/tax forms) or a PO-only process? Any required vendor IDs?
4) Timeline: target date for internal procurement sign-off for pilot? (helps us plan listing/onboarding)

What I’m attaching
- procurement-checklist.pdf (short checklist you can share with finance/procurement)

Suggested next steps
- If Marketplace: I’ll loop in Karthik (sales ops) to outline the SKU/metering and typical listing timeline.
- If PO: please share your PO template + expected SLA/payment terms so we can surface to finance.
- Quick follow-up call: propose Tue, Jul 6, 10:00 AM PT to align procurement + technical onboarding.

If helpful, feel free to send a short note with your preferred path and procurement contact details and we’ll build the mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0173

[attachment: procurement-checklist.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudscale.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@cloudscale.io>
Date: Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 1:45 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement route & marketplace preference (CloudScale Analytics)

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the recap and the checklist. A few notes from procurement side:

- Preference: AWS Marketplace preferred for this engagement. It significantly shortens our vendor onboarding and is required for several internal approvals.
- Timeline: Procurement will need to review commercial terms and the Marketplace listing metadata — expecting an internal review window up to July 15.
- PO vs Card: For pilots we can often run on a corporate card, but our security/compliance team prefers Marketplace billing for anything that becomes a subscribed product.
- Requirements: I’m attaching our approval matrix (shows who needs to sign off at what dollar thresholds) and our vendor onboarding checklist.

Questions for Redwood:
- Do you have an AWS Marketplace SKU we can reference now? If not, can you provide expected SKU naming and pricing granularity (hourly vs monthly vs token-based)?
- Are trial credits or a short-term pilot price available via Marketplace?

We’ll loop in our finance contact (Tom) if we proceed with a PO.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Procurement | CloudScale Analytics
lena.ortiz@cloudscale.io | +1 (206) 555-0199

[attachment: cloudscale-approval-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 60 KB)]

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, Jul 1, 2027 at 10:03 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement route & marketplace preference (CloudScale Analytics)

Hi Lena —

Looping in with the marketplace and billing details — happy to run this with your procurement team. Short answers up front:

- Marketplace SKU: We don’t yet have a live SKU for CloudScale specifically, but we can provide the planned SKU mapping and pricing bands for the pilot. I’ve attached a CSV with the SKU templates we typically publish (metered by usage/token blocks or monthly subscription).
- Pilot billing: You can run the pilot on a corporate card for the first 30 days; if you want Marketplace-native billing (to appear in your AWS invoices) we can prioritize the listing but that process typically takes 2-3 weeks for onboarding and verification.
- PO path: We accept PO (Net 30) for Dedicated/Private engagements under an enterprise contract. For pilots under $X, we usually recommend card or Marketplace subscription. If you need a PO for the pilot specifically, please share the PO template and we’ll confirm vendor paperwork (W9/tax info).

Technical/ops notes:
- Marketplace listing will require a minimal set of artifacts: product description, SKU CSV, support contact, and a simple usage dimension (we recommend token-metered usage to match your billing model).
- For VPC/private deployment later, billing still proceeds via the Marketplace or direct invoicing depending on the purchase path you choose.

Next steps I can own
- Provide a draft SKU CSV and expected price bands (attached: aws-marketplace-sku.csv).
- Help coordinate seller onboarding with our marketplace specialist — we’ll need a point of contact from your procurement side for the registration steps.

Proposed timeline
- Jul 6: short sync (30m) to align procurement items and agree on pilot billing path
- Jul 12: aim to have pilot access and trial credits enabled if Marketplace path chosen

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sales Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0122
